title: Is PIP reaching the right people?
gist: A Resolution Foundation weekly newsletter ahead of the UK Budget: PIP survey evidence that 12% of recipients report neither higher limitations nor higher costs, a Budget preview with borrowing about 10 billion pounds higher and headroom halving to 12 billion, plus IMF, Norway wealth-tax and French minimum-wage findings.

insights.claim: The Resolution Foundation expects the OBR's pre-decision forecast to show borrowing about 10 billion pounds a year higher than in Spring, driven mainly by higher debt interest costs from global bond market jitters.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Higher gilt yields feeding debt interest worsen UK fiscal arithmetic; watch gilt supply and tax-rise odds.

insights.claim: Headroom against the fiscal rule to balance day-to-day spending with tax in 2029-30 is expected to halve from 24 billion pounds to 12 billion pounds, versus the IFS forecast of 20 billion, with the gap mainly due to a higher wage forecast.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: The OBR's wage forecast is a key swing factor for headroom and thus Budget tax measures.

insights.claim: If its headroom estimate is right, the Chancellor is expected to raise some taxes in 2029-30 to move closer to the IFS's 20 billion pound headroom figure.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Expect back-loaded tax increases in the Budget; positioning for gilts and domestic-facing sectors.

insights.claim: A typical UK family is estimated to be 2,900 pounds worse off than if the cost of living crisis had not happened, with energy bills forecast to reach nearly 2,000 pounds a year in January and almost one in five households in the poorer half already behind on priority bills.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Pressure for cost-of-living support in the Budget competes with fiscal repair.

insights.claim: The Budget's central tension is balancing medium-term repair of public finances against immediate cost-of-living support for vulnerable households, with public spending path decisions left unresolved.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Expect a limited, not blockbuster, fiscal event; watch for targeted support funded by later tax rises.

insights.claim: The IMF raised its UK growth forecast for this year by 0.5 percentage points to 1.3 per cent, the joint-largest upgrade in the G7, and projects the deficit shrinking to 1.4 per cent of GDP by 2031, the biggest fall in borrowing in the G7.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Supportive headline for UK fiscal credibility.

insights.claim: On GDP per capita, the measure that matters most for living standards, the UK is set to grow just 0.7 per cent this year, so the IMF's headline upgrade overstates the improvement in living standards.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Population growth flatters aggregate GDP; judge UK strength on per-capita terms.

insights.claim: Chancellor John Healey has apparently rejected calls to equalise Capital Gains Tax with Income Tax.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Reduces odds of CGT alignment in the Budget.

insights.claim: Norway's 2021-2024 wealth tax reforms doubled the top marginal tax rate on business wealth, raised dividend taxes by 6 percentage points and closed exit-tax loopholes.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Evidence base for wealth-tax design debates.

insights.claim: Despite headlines of wealthy people fleeing to Switzerland, at most 100 people left Norway, largely before the exit-tax loophole closed, and there was no reduced inflow of startup founders or inventors.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Undercuts the capital-flight argument against wealth taxes.

insights.claim: Norway's wealth tax receipts rose 71.5 per cent after the reforms, versus 75 per cent growth had the departing taxpayers stayed, with no hit to economic activity and investment.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Suggests small revenue leakage from emigration.

insights.claim: The UK is internationally unusual in having no exit tax at all.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: A possible UK policy lever if wealth taxation expands.

insights.claim: In a Resolution Foundation survey, 12 per cent of PIP recipients report neither higher limitations nor higher extra costs, so on the benefit's own terms they may not be the intended cohort.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Fuels the case for better targeting of disability benefits.
insights.quote: One-in-eight (12 per cent) report neither higher limitations nor higher costs

insights.claim: Almost half (44 per cent) of PIP recipients with neither higher limitations nor higher costs are under 35, compared with a quarter (26 per cent) of the remaining caseload.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Age skew guides where reform and scrutiny may focus.

insights.claim: 31 per cent of PIP recipients without higher limitations or costs receive a higher PIP award, indicating the assessment is not reliably identifying the right cohort.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Assessment redesign is a likely reform theme.

insights.claim: The scope to save money simply by excluding certain conditions from PIP is very limited, so quick fixes are not available.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Tempers expectations of large welfare savings from condition-based eligibility cuts.

insights.claim: The Resolution Foundation argues PIP should become more flexible to disabled people's needs and more focused on their participation in society, based on a survey of 2,500 recipients.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Signals the direction of think-tank proposals on welfare reform.

insights.claim: When French firms faced a minimum-wage employee cost increase of 3.7 per cent from the 35-hour week reforms, employment fell only 0.9 per cent and revenue per job rose 1.1 per cent.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Modest disemployment from wage floors supports minimum-wage increases.

insights.claim: Firms facing higher wage floors responded by training lowest-paid staff, stripping out management layers and holding down pay higher up the ladder, rather than mainly firing workers.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Wage floors reshape internal hierarchies and compress wage distributions.

insights.claim: European survey data show a predicted height difference of 2 to 5 cm between the top and bottom of the social class and income distributions, particularly dependent on childhood financial hardship.
insights.speaker: Resolution Foundation
insights.so_what: Height remains a living-standards proxy, but it is a Substack analysis.
